name: LogiQA
ability_definition: The ability to apply general rules to specific problems to produce answers that make sense.

task_realism.reasoning: The questions come from Chinese civil-service exams, which were written to screen people for government jobs. They do test applying stated rules and premises to reach necessary conclusions. However, they are short, self-contained puzzles. Real workplace deduction means applying policies, regulations, codes, diagnostic criteria or specifications to messy, detailed cases. LogiQA passages are toy-like and lack domain substance, ambiguity and consequences. Translation from Chinese also introduces awkward phrasing unlike real work text.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Models are fine-tuned on an in-distribution training split and tested on a clean, closed test set. Each item has all premises given and exactly one correct answer. There are no tools, no reference documents to search, no need to find which rules apply, no follow-up and no stakes. Real work often requires identifying the relevant rule from a large body of material, dealing with incomplete information, and justifying conclusions to others. None of that is present, and the fine-tuning setup rewards learning the dataset's patterns rather than general deductive skill.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It covers several formal deduction types: categorical, conditional, disjunctive and conjunctive reasoning, plus some constraint-satisfaction and assignment puzzles. That is a reasonable slice of the core logic. But some items fall outside strict deduction, such as assumption-finding and weakening. More importantly, it only measures recognizing a valid conclusion among options. It does not measure generating a conclusion, applying rules across long or technical contexts, handling exceptions and conflicting rules, or checking whether an answer makes practical sense.

format_match.reasoning: The format is forced four-option multiple choice over a short paragraph. Workplace deduction produces decisions, determinations, written justifications, compliance judgments or diagnoses, usually with no candidate answers supplied. Multiple choice also allows answering by eliminating options, and it does not resemble any real work artifact.

transferability_reasoning: LogiQA faithfully targets the logical core of deductive reasoning with expert-written exam items, but it isolates that core in short, decontextualized puzzles. Models are fine-tuned on in-distribution data and answer by choosing from four options. Strong LogiQA performance is weak-to-moderate evidence of the ability to apply real rules, policies and specifications to messy workplace cases and produce sensible, justified answers.

2020.metric: accuracy (%) on LogiQA test set, 4-way multiple choice
2020.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: adults who take civil-service-style logical reasoning tests and do rule-application reasoning at work, such as college-educated applicants and professionals.

2021.metric: accuracy (%) on the LogiQA test set, 4-option multiple choice
2021.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: typical adults who take or do work comparable to Chinese civil-service logical-reasoning sections, such as administrative and analytical staff.
